item.title: AI Prompt Leaks, Azure API Credential Theft, and KEPCO Data Breach
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Nov 19:00 → 23 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials — Must Read

Microsoft fixed an actively exploited flaw in Azure API Management Classic that could let unauthorized actors access stored secrets, subscription keys, and management tokens. Affected customers must rotate potentially exposed credentials and investigate for misuse, as the fix does not revoke credentials stolen before remediation.

  • Microsoft said an exploited vulnerability in Azure API Management Classic tiers could allow unauthorized parties to access stored secrets and perform administrative operations when instances were not configured according to recommended security practices.
  • Potentially exposed information included Named Values secrets, identity and OpenID Connect client secrets, subscription keys, and tokens for direct management APIs.
  • Microsoft identified the issue on November 18, 2026, closed the unauthorized access path on November 19, and rotated Microsoft-controlled credentials where appropriate.
  • Microsoft warned that its remediation does not automatically invalidate customer credentials that may have been accessed before the fix, and urged affected customers to rotate them and review systems and logs for suspicious activity.
  • Norway's National Security Authority linked the issue to incidents affecting Norwegian organizations, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi, while stating that organizations in other countries and sectors were also affected.

Technologies: api-gateway, secrets-manager, cloud-platform

Products: azure-api-management-classic, azure-key-vault

Vendors: microsoft

South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million — Should Read

South Korea’s state-controlled power utility KEPCO confirmed that attackers accessed its billing and procurement systems, exposing personal and financial information for more than 1.5 million customers, employees, and company representatives. A threat actor using the alias Noiem claimed responsibility, though attribution remains unconfirmed.

  • Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) confirmed unauthorized access to its KEPCO ON electricity billing platform and its SRM electronic procurement system on November 20.
  • The incident exposed data belonging to more than 1.5 million people, including 650,487 KEPCO ON customers, 426,827 company representatives, and 442,934 KEPCO employees.
  • Exposed customer information included names, identification details, contact and address information, bank and payment-card details, and electricity billing information.
  • KEPCO blocked external IP access, suspended the affected services, and is directly notifying affected individuals while coordinating with data-protection, government, and financial authorities.
  • A threat actor using the alias Noiem claimed the breach and said it possessed KEPCO user, supplier, bidding, and contract data, but attribution remains unconfirmed.

Products: kepco-on, srm

Vendors: korea-electric-power-corporation

Dragos Canary Research: AI Data Security Risks | Cyera — Should Read

Dragos researchers found that AI prompts—including those marked for zero data retention—were exposed through compromised inference providers, marketplace resellers, and undisclosed routing paths. Organizations should treat every prompt as external data exposure, restrict provider routing, prevent credentials from entering agent context, and retain prompt audit trails for incident response.

  • Dragos researchers embedded unique trackable secrets in about two million prompts sent to widely used AI services and reported that prompts were retained, shared with other companies, and read by people.
  • The research found attackers inside three AI hosting providers, including an incident in which attackers captured requests at a provider entry point and used stolen AWS keys to make tens of thousands of AWS API calls.
  • Dragos observed marketplace resellers opening secret URLs and manually attempting passwords from customer prompts, while one Chinese AI lab opened secret links from about two-thirds of requests marked for zero data retention or no data collection.
  • OpenRouter said on November 22 that it removed three providers and 125 endpoints from zero-data-retention eligibility, while stating that its findings showed no breach of OpenRouter itself.
  • The article recommends restricting routing for sensitive AI work, inspecting prompts and agent tool results for credentials before they leave, using canary credentials, and retaining records of agent activity.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, secrets-manager, api-gateway, dlp

Products: openrouter, amazon-bedrock, amazon-s3, aws-secrets-manager, aws-systems-manager-parameter-store, cyera-ai-firewall

Vendors: dragos, openrouter, phala, atlas-cloud, novita, together-ai, amazon-web-services, cyera

Hardened container images: STIGs, FIPS and FedRAMP explained — Optional

Hardened container images reduce attack surface by removing unnecessary components and enforcing secure configurations against baselines such as DISA STIGs, while FIPS separately governs use of validated cryptographic modules. FedRAMP requires hardened, regularly scanned images and pipeline enforcement, but these practices benefit any organization seeking stronger container security.

  • A hardened container image removes software the application does not need, such as shells, package managers, and compilers, and locks down the remaining configuration.
  • DISA STIGs are U.S. Department of Defense configuration standards with individual checks that can be tested and documented, including checks that do not apply to containers because they are handled by the host.
  • FIPS 140 concerns validated cryptographic modules and does not by itself harden a container image or ensure that every application component uses approved cryptography.
  • FedRAMP requires container images to be hardened against a benchmark from NIST’s National Checklist Program, scanned before deployment, and assessed within the previous 30 days before running in production.
  • Minimal, distroless, and scratch images can reduce attack surface, but they do not necessarily meet a defined secure-configuration baseline.

Technologies: container-platform, operating-system, ci-cd

Products: aikido-images, rhel, red-hat-ubi, ubuntu, oracle-linux, debian, alpine-linux, rocky-linux, openscap, openssl

Vendors: aikido-security, red-hat, canonical, oracle, debian-project, alpine-linux, rocky-linux, openscap, openssl-project

SASE in the Age of AI: Why Architecture Matters More Than Ever — Optional

AI and autonomous agents dramatically increase traffic, operational dependency, and security risks, but SASE’s core distributed, edge-delivered zero-trust architecture remains the right foundation. Organizations should prioritize globally distributed, single-pass SASE implementations with continuous, context-aware inspection rather than treating SASE as a checklist of features.

  • The article argues that AI increases security and networking demands because users now include both people and autonomous agents that generate large volumes of globally distributed traffic.
  • It warns that large numbers of autonomous agents can cause data leaks, proprietary-model theft, compliance violations, cost overruns, and malicious code or threats.
  • The author says SASE should remain primarily cloud delivered and highly distributed, while acknowledging that some desktop-based agents may require on-premises controls.
  • The article recommends least-privilege access with continuous context- and behavior-based monitoring of agents, including detailed inspection of API and JSON transactions.
  • It argues that edge-based, single-pass traffic delivery is needed for data sovereignty, consistent performance, and time-sensitive AI applications.

Technologies: casb

item.title: Microsoft Azure API Management Flaw, Webworm SoftEther Modifications, and FBI NCIC Breach Reports
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Nov 15:00 → 23 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Norway says hackers exploited Microsoft security flaw to attack energy firms Equinor, Skagerak Energi — Must Read

Hackers exploited a flaw in Microsoft Azure API Management Classic tiers to target credentials at Norwegian energy firms Equinor and Skagerak Energi, though neither reported operational disruption or confirmed data theft. Microsoft says it fixed the issue, notified affected customers, and advised credential rotation.

  • Norway’s National Security Authority said an unidentified threat actor actively targeted access tokens and other sensitive information through a flaw in Microsoft Azure API Management.
  • Equinor and Skagerak Energi reported cyberattacks, but both said their energy operations continued normally and they found no indication that data or information had been compromised.
  • Microsoft said the issue affected older Azure API Management Classic tiers and that it closed the access path on November 19 after discovering it on November 18.
  • Microsoft warned that passwords and other sensitive information may have been accessed in vulnerable Azure API Management systems before the issue was fixed.
  • Norwegian authorities said organizations across multiple sectors in Norway and abroad were affected and urged Azure API Management users to take protective steps.

Technologies: api-gateway, secrets-manager, cloud-platform

Products: azure-api-management, azure-key-vault

Vendors: microsoft

FBI reportedly facing second data breach involving National Crime Information Center — Should Read

The FBI is investigating a reported breach of the National Crime Information Center, a sensitive law-enforcement database containing warrant, fugitive, criminal, and missing-person records. If confirmed, it would be the FBI’s second major cyber incident of the year.

  • The FBI is reportedly investigating a cyberattack involving the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), according to sources cited by CNN and the Associated Press.
  • The NCIC is used by local, state, and federal law-enforcement agencies to share information on criminals and investigations, including outstanding warrants.
  • President Donald Trump said he had been briefed on the incident and described it as "not good."
  • If confirmed, the NCIC incident would be the second cybersecurity incident affecting the FBI this year, following the alleged September breach of the FBI’s job site by ShinyHunters.
  • Other U.S. government entities, including federal bankruptcy courts, the ATF, the Departments of Defense and Transportation, and the Department of Agriculture, also experienced cybersecurity incidents this year.

Technologies: database

Products: national-crime-information-center

Vendors: federal-bureau-of-investigation

Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access — Should Read

China-aligned Webworm is suspected of rebuilding SoftEther VPN Bridge as “NtMonitor VPN” to remove recognizable fingerprints and conceal covert remote access. The modified tool changes HTTP endpoints, handshake watermarks, and configuration storage for stealth rather than adding new capabilities.

  • Rapid7 assessed with moderate confidence that the China-aligned Webworm group is using a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge to conceal remote access to compromised networks.
  • The Windows executable netcapa.exe is based on SoftEther VPN Bridge version 4.44 build 9807 and is rebranded as “NtMonitor VPN,” presenting itself as Network Monitor Software.
  • The altered tool replaces SoftEther’s usual HTTP endpoints and GIF-based handshake marker with ordinary-looking endpoints and a PNG-based marker to evade detection signatures.
  • The modified build renames and encrypts its configuration file as setting.conf, which begins with the ASCII magic bytes “RCEN.”
  • Rapid7 found no new functionality in the modified tool, indicating that its changes are focused on stealth rather than added capabilities.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access, network-monitoring

Products: softether-vpn, softether-vpn-bridge, ntmonitor-vpn

Vendors: softether-project, rapid7

CrowdStrike to purchase Zscaler for $43.9 billion — Should Read

CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, combining CrowdStrike’s endpoint and threat-response capabilities with Zscaler’s cloud and zero-trust network security portfolio.

  • CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valued at $43.9 billion.
  • Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share, valued at $260.41 per share.
  • Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading Zscaler and join CrowdStrike’s board of directors.
  • CrowdStrike said the deal will add network security capabilities and extend its offerings to Zscaler’s 8,000 customers, including 50% of the Fortune 500.
  • Zscaler reported first-quarter revenue of $949.3 million, a 20% increase from the prior year’s first quarter.

Technologies: edr, xdr, casb, cloud-platform

Products: crowdstrike-falcon, zscaler-zero-trust-exchange, wiz-cloud-security-platform

Vendors: crowdstrike, zscaler, google, wiz

Signal blocks screenshots by Apple, Google operating systems to protect data from AI agents — May Read

Signal will block screenshots by default on certain Apple and Google operating systems when AI agents may read screen content, citing risks to message privacy. Users can disable the restriction, but Signal says stronger OS-level controls and documentation are needed to prevent AI agents from accessing app data.

  • Signal plans to block screenshots of messages by default on certain Apple and Google operating systems where it detects AI assistants trying to read on-screen text.
  • The company says the change is intended to limit the risk that operating-system AI agents scan Signal conversations and make captured data available to local databases or remote servers.
  • Users will be able to disable the screenshot restriction in Signal’s settings.
  • Signal says blocking screenshots is incomplete because AI agents could potentially access content already on a device through the file system.
  • Signal called on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide clearer documentation and controls that let users and app developers limit AI-agent access to application data.

Technologies: mobile-os, operating-system

Products: signal, gemini-intelligence, siri-ai, ios-27, android, windows-11, macos, muse

Vendors: signal-foundation, apple, google, microsoft, meta

⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble — Optional

This weekly recap highlights widespread exploitation and high-impact flaws across VMware vCenter, cloud platforms, routers, AI tools, and major software stacks, showing how stolen credentials, trusted services, and unpatched systems enable rapid compromise. Organizations should urgently prioritize the listed critical CVEs, rotate exposed credentials, and investigate potentially persistent infections after patching.

  • A suspected China-linked espionage group called Armory Castle exploited a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication-bypass zero-day, CVE-2026-123890, in early September 2026.
  • Cursor said that a malicious Claude Code extension in its marketplace was traced to an exposed access key issued to Fireworks, which an attacker used to copy data from a shared read-only storage bucket.
  • GL.iNet said attackers exploited a GoodCloud cloud-management vulnerability to install malicious software on some customer routers and KVM devices, and that cloud-side fixes do not remove malware from already infected devices.
  • Researchers showed that an attacker-controlled web page could access Meta Muse conversation histories and stored memories and escape its runtime container to gain root privileges in the underlying virtual machine; Meta has addressed the issue.
  • The article lists numerous high-severity vulnerabilities affecting widely used products, including Java, NGINX, F5 BIG-IP, Docker Model Runner, Ruby, Google Chrome, Drupal, VMware, and WhatsApp.

Technologies: hypervisor, remote-access, cloud-platform, operating-system, router, web-server, load-balancer, container-platform, browser

Products: vmware-vcenter-server, vmware-directory-service, beyondtrust-remote-support, claude-code, meta-muse, windows-11, goodcloud, nginx, nginx-plus, big-ip, java, ruby, google-chrome, docker-model-runner

Vendors: broadcom, f5, oracle, meta, gl-inet, microsoft, google, cursor, fireworks-ai, anthropic, asus, n-able

OMB M-26-14: Network Evidence for Federal Agencies | Corelight — Optional

Corelight promotes network evidence as a way for U.S. federal agencies to meet OMB M-26-14 cybersecurity requirements, emphasizing continuous network visibility and forensic readiness.

  • The article is titled "OMB M-26-14: Network Evidence for Federal Agencies."
  • The article concerns OMB M-26-14.

item.title: Critical ScreenConnect, Mail Assure, and binary-parser Flaws Drive Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Nov 11:00 → 23 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting the critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 to silently push and execute malicious files on MSP technicians’ workstations, enabling remote takeover and access to customer environments. Organizations should update ScreenConnect host clients to version 26.6.5 or later and investigate potentially exposed technician systems.

  • Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect client flaw with a CVSS score of 9.9, to transfer and execute files on a connecting technician’s host.
  • Huntress observed an MSP technician workstation run a guest-pushed batch file that contacted a Telegram bot, downloaded a Windows-update-themed MSI installer, and launched a rogue ScreenConnect client within about nine seconds.
  • Between October 20 and November 16, 2026, Huntress recorded at least 688,000 guest “run file” requests targeting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses.
  • Huntress also identified 2,408 unauthorized ScreenConnect guest sessions across at least 118 self-hosted servers belonging to 109 protected organizations, with many using cryptocurrency exchange-themed names.
  • Organizations are advised to update technician ScreenConnect host clients to version 26.6.5 or later, or remove the TransferFiles permission if patching cannot occur immediately.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: screenconnect, screenconnect-access, sckit

Vendors: connectwise, huntress, telegram, ionos

N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation — Should Read

N-able fixed a critical SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-134624) in its Mail Assure/SpamExperts Hosted Cloud platform after investigating an unauthorized server access incident. The company says no customer data compromise has been found, but customers must replace revoked API and OAuth credentials.

  • N-able disclosed CVE-2026-134624, a critical server-side request forgery flaw in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email-filtering service.
  • The flaw allowed authenticated users with high-level API access to make the platform connect to chosen internal hosts and ports and send crafted data to internal services.
  • N-able patched the issue in build 20261121.1943 and restored dashboard and API access late Saturday after an outage that began the previous Monday.
  • During the incident response, N-able took an affected Hosted Cloud server offline, rotated internal credentials, revoked customer API and OAuth tokens, and reset local user passwords.
  • N-able says it has found no evidence of customer-data compromise or exploitation beyond one server, and its investigation remains ongoing.

Technologies: email-security, network-monitoring

Products: mail-assure, spamexperts-hosted-cloud, spamexperts-local-cloud, n-central

Vendors: n-able

Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions — Should Read

Binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 have a critical code-injection flaw (CVE-2026-134814) that can let attackers who control parser definitions execute arbitrary JavaScript in Node.js during parser compilation. Users should upgrade to version 2.3.1 or later.

  • Binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 contain CVE-2026-134814, a code-injection flaw that can allow arbitrary JavaScript execution when an attacker controls parser definitions.
  • The flaw stems from string options such as length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, and aliases passed to namely() being inserted into generated JavaScript without adequate validation.
  • The vulnerability is triggered when a crafted parser definition is compiled in a Node.js process, not simply by parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition.
  • The binary-parser maintainer stated that version 2.3.1 validates these options as identifier paths and rejects expressions such as "len - 1."
  • CVE-2026-134814 is described as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-1245, an earlier code-injection issue involving insufficient validation of field names and encoding parameters.

Products: binary-parser, node-js

Vendors: binary-parser, github, nist

Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans — May Read

A Peruvian call-center operator received an eight-year U.S. prison sentence for running a government-impersonation scam that defrauded more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking U.S. residents of roughly $15 million.

  • Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza, a Peruvian call center operator, was sentenced to eight years in prison after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud.
  • Alcedo managed Peruvian call centers linked to fraud and extortion schemes between January 2013 and December 2018.
  • The scheme targeted Spanish-speaking U.S. residents with calls falsely claiming they owed money and threats of court action, arrest, and immigration consequences.
  • The U.S. Department of Justice said the scheme defrauded more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking U.S. residents of $15 million.
  • The Federal Trade Commission reported that Americans lost $3.5 billion to impersonation scams in 2025, including about $920 million to government impersonators.

Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops — May Read

Microsoft is testing a Windows 11 fix that lets compatible Bluetooth LE Audio headsets maintain full-quality stereo sound while their microphone is active, addressing the longstanding quality drop caused by switching to hands-free audio mode.

  • Microsoft is testing a Windows 11 fix intended to prevent Bluetooth audio quality from dropping when an application uses a headset microphone.
  • The quality drop occurs when Windows switches from the stereo headphone mode to a call-focused headset mode with limited two-way audio capacity.
  • Windows 11 Insiders in the Beta and Experimental channels can test full-range stereo playback with microphone use on compatible Bluetooth LE Audio devices.
  • Users with a PC supporting Super Wideband Stereo can select a new two-channel, 16-bit, 48 kHz audio format when the microphone is active.
  • The feature supports Bluetooth LE Audio headphones, earbuds, and speakers that support 48 kHz playback.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-11, windows-11-24h2, intel-smart-sound-technology

Vendors: microsoft, intel

item.title: Active Exploitation Targets Cisco Expressway, Idunno.AntiCsrf, and GL.iNet GoodCloud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Nov 07:00 → 23 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks — Must Read

CISA added CVE-2026-76466, a critical Cisco Expressway flaw that enables unauthenticated root-level remote code execution on clustered devices, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after evidence of active attacks. Organizations should urgently apply Cisco’s patches, particularly for Internet-exposed Expressway systems.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-76466, a critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog after identifying active exploitation.
  • The flaw affects clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E devices and can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute operating-system commands as root because of hard-coded credentials and incomplete client-certificate validation.
  • CISA ordered U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to secure affected systems within three days under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 and urged all organizations to prioritize patching.
  • F6 reported that attackers compromised two internet-facing Cisco Expressway devices, used one to reach two additional internal cluster nodes, and then prepared tools for movement across the network.
  • Cisco stated when it released patches in late October that its PSIRT was not aware of active exploitation or public proof-of-concept exploits for CVE-2026-76466.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: cisco-expressway, cisco-expressway-c, cisco-expressway-e

Vendors: cisco, f6, malbear-labs

Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE — Must Read

A critical, actively exploited insecure deserialization flaw in the abandoned Idunno.AntiCsrf ASP.NET library lets unauthenticated attackers execute code on affected IIS servers with a single crafted POST request. Organizations should immediately remove the library, migrate to a supported anti-CSRF mechanism, and investigate for compromise.

  • CVE-2026-131914 is a critical insecure deserialization flaw, rated CVSS 9.3, affecting Idunno.AntiCsrf versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta.
  • The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on an affected ASP.NET WebForms server through a single crafted HTTP POST request.
  • Google Mandiant reported that the vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild.
  • Idunno.AntiCsrf is an abandoned third-party ASP.NET anti-CSRF library that has not been updated since December 2008.
  • Organizations are advised to discontinue Idunno.AntiCsrf, use a supported anti-CSRF alternative, and review IIS logs and webroots for evidence of exploitation.

Technologies: web-server

Products: idunno-anticrsf, asp-net-webforms, microsoft-iis, asp-net-core-antiforgery, system-web-helpers-antiforgery

Vendors: idunno, microsoft, google, mandiant

Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices — Should Read

Attackers exploited a GL.iNet GoodCloud flaw to remotely run root-level commands and install malware on some routers and KVM devices. GL.iNet has patched the cloud service and released security firmware, but affected owners should update immediately and consider reinstalling firmware without preserving settings because prior compromise may expose credentials and persist.

  • Attackers exploited a flaw in GL.iNet’s GoodCloud remote-management service to install malware on some customer routers and KVM devices.
  • GL.iNet said it fixed the cloud-side flaw and blocked the attacker’s access, but already infected devices require owners to check their hardware and install the listed security firmware.
  • RemoteToHome Consulting verified a root-level remote command connection on a GL-AXT1800 router running firmware 4.8.3 with GoodCloud enabled.
  • GL.iNet’s published firmware updates are intended to remove malware identified in this incident without a factory reset, while researchers caution that a root-level intruder may have left behind additional changes.
  • Owners of devices showing signs of compromise are advised by researchers to reinstall firmware without keeping settings and treat saved passwords, keys, and cloud credentials as exposed.

Technologies: router, remote-access, cloud-platform, iot-device

Products: goodcloud, astrowarp, gl-axt1800, gl-mt6000, gl-rm1, gl-mt3000, gl-rmq1

Vendors: gl-inet

Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users — May Read

Microsoft says Windows 11 24H2-and-later devices using Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent may be unable to print after installing the KB5132043 November 2026 hotpatch because the Print Spooler service can fail to start. The issue is limited to hotpatch updates delivered through Windows Autopatch, and Forcepoint has provided a temporary workaround while Microsoft works on a fix.

  • Microsoft confirmed that the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch KB5132043 can cause printing failures on Windows 11 24H2 and later devices running Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent.
  • Affected users may find the print option disabled or receive printer-selection errors because the Windows Print Spooler service fails to start.
  • The issue applies to hotpatch updates deployed through Windows Autopatch and does not affect systems using the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.
  • Forcepoint has published a temporary workaround for customers through its support portal, while Microsoft has not yet released a fix.
  • Microsoft also reported that KB5132043 can cause application installation and launch problems affecting Office and third-party applications.

Technologies: operating-system, dlp, iam, cloud-platform

Products: windows-11, forcepoint-dlp-endpoint-agent, windows-autopatch, microsoft-intune, microsoft-graph-api, windows-server-2016

Vendors: microsoft, forcepoint

Black Friday, red flags: too-good-to-be-true deals hiding real threats — Optional

Kaspersky reports a sharp rise in shopping-related phishing and Black Friday spam in 2026, with scammers heavily impersonating Amazon, Apple, Netflix and other trusted brands to steal credentials, payment data and money. Shoppers should treat urgent, unusually cheap offers and unsolicited links with skepticism and verify retailers directly before entering personal or payment information.

  • From January through October 2026, Kaspersky blocked 19,063,077 phishing-link access attempts targeting users of online stores, payment systems, and banks, a 198.1% increase from the same period in 2025.
  • Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Shopify, and Alibaba Group-associated brands accounted for 7,119,400 phishing detections, representing 83.83% of phishing targeting online stores and subscription services.
  • Kaspersky detected 220,071 sales-season spam messages during the first two weeks of November 2026, 50.18% more than during the comparable period in 2025.
  • Between June and November 2026, Kaspersky detected 27,416 attacks involving malware or potentially unwanted applications disguised as GTA VI-related content.
  • Kaspersky recorded 801,150 banking-Trojan attacks in the first ten months of 2026, down from more than 1.09 million in 2025.

Technologies: antivirus

Products: kaspersky-premium, amazon, apple-pay, netflix, shopify, aliexpress, google-play, steam, discord

Vendors: kaspersky, amazon, apple, netflix, shopify, alibaba-group, google, valve, discord

AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks and Fintech Firms — Optional

India's CERT-In warns that AI-assisted cyberattacks are enabling criminals to manipulate business records and trusted approval workflows, resulting in unauthorized payments at banks, fintechs, and government-linked service providers. The activity illustrates how agentic offensive frameworks can rapidly automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and intrusion tasks while evading controls designed around conventional attacks.

  • CERT-In warned that AI-assisted attacks have caused unauthorized financial transactions at Indian banking and financial-services organizations, government-linked payment service providers, and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts.
  • In observed incidents, attackers altered business records or approval relationships and then used legitimate payment workflows, exploiting gaps in independent verification, reconciliation, and review.
  • CERT-In said agentic offensive frameworks have been used for automated reconnaissance, rapid exploit generation, parallel intrusion tasks, and adaptation to blocked attempts or returned information.
  • The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre said attacks against banks, non-banking financial companies, and fintech firms led to multi-crore unauthorized transactions through fund-disbursement systems and payment-transfer APIs.
  • The article reports that frameworks such as ARTEX coordinate specialized AI agents across stages including system discovery, initial access, privilege escalation, internal movement, and data theft.

Products: artex, pentagi, cairn, cyberstrikeai, exploit-agent, hermes, antifox

item.title: Ransomware Affiliates Weigh AI Pentesting Tools Against Operational Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 19:00 → 22 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Top Ransomware Gangs & AI Pentesting Tools — Optional

Top ransomware affiliates have not broadly adopted autonomous AI pentesting frameworks because their proven access-broker model and manual Windows/ESXi tradecraft are stealthier, more reliable, and more cost-effective. AI is more likely being used quietly for operator assistance, while smaller crews absorb the expense and OPSEC risks of agentic tooling.

  • The article says established ransomware affiliates such as Akira, Qilin, and Rhysida have not been widely reported using autonomous AI offensive frameworks such as ARTEX, Cairn, or PentAGI.
  • Smaller or newer extortion groups, including WhiteArmor, Settra, and n0n, have been observed experimenting with AI tools, sometimes with poor operational security.
  • Top ransomware affiliates often purchase pre-vetted corporate access from initial access brokers and focus on internal actions such as moving through Windows domains, stealing data, and targeting VMware ESXi systems.
  • The article argues that cloud-based AI services can create logging, account-suspension, attribution, and cost risks, while locally hosting capable models requires expensive hardware and operational effort.
  • SOCRadar reported cases involving INC/Lynx and TheGentlemen affiliates using AI-based frameworks, with reported OpenRouter costs of $4,500 and $23,900 respectively.

Technologies: firewall, hypervisor, iam, orchestration

Products: artex, cairn, cyberstrikeai, pentagi, phantom, fortigate, vmware-esxi, claude-opus, opencode, active-directory

Vendors: fortinet, vmware, openrouter, anthropic, microsoft

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Compromise, Cleverbridge Card Theft, and Signal AI Privacy Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 15:00 → 22 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices — Should Read

Attackers exploited a flaw in GL.iNet’s GoodCloud remote-management service to install persistent malware and reverse shells on routers and KVM devices, potentially exposing connected systems. GL.iNet has blocked the attack path and urges customers to update firmware, scan devices, preserve evidence, reset compromised systems, and rotate credentials.

item.title: OpenRouter Prompt Theft and Ghostscript CVE-2026-125396 Sandbox Escape
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 03:00 → 22 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms — Should Read

Dragos found that attackers and unscrupulous AI inference providers had been copying customer prompts, including Zero Data Retention requests, for months, exposing credentials and sensitive data. OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility while notifying potentially affected users.

  • Dragos seeded roughly two million AI prompts with unique links and credentials between July and November and found evidence that data from three AI inference providers had been copied for months.
  • Some copied requests were marked Zero Data Retention, a setting intended to ensure that prompts are not stored.
  • OpenRouter said it removed three providers from its platform, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, and notified potentially affected customers.
  • Researchers observed attackers using stolen planted AWS keys to list S3 buckets, search AWS Secrets Manager and Parameter Store, and attempt to create Bedrock API keys and IAM users.
  • Phala, Together AI, and Novita each publicly disclosed separate incidents involving exposure, storage, or unintended forwarding of customer AI requests.

Technologies: api-gateway, cloud-platform, object-storage, secrets-manager

Products: openrouter, artex, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, minimax-m3, glm-5-2, kimi-k2-6, amazon-s3, aws-secrets-manager, amazon-bedrock, feishu

Vendors: openrouter, dragos, phala, together-ai, novita, minimax, deepseek, amazon-web-services, feishu

Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps — Should Read

A patched Ghostscript use-after-free flaw (CVE-2026-125396) lets crafted uploaded documents bypass the -dSAFER sandbox and execute commands on servers through common rendering paths in apps such as WordPress, Roundcube, and ImageMagick. Organizations should update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or later, including copies embedded in containers and application bundles.

  • Ghostscript flaw CVE-2026-125396 allowed crafted files to bypass its -dSAFER protections and run commands on the server processing them.
  • The issue was a use-after-free bug in Ghostscript's font-loading code, and Artifex fixed it in Ghostscript version 10.08.0 on September 8.
  • pwn.ai demonstrated that upload, preview, and print features in about ten applications could route crafted PostScript or EPS content to Ghostscript, including through image and document libraries.
  • Some tested paths required no login, including anonymous jobs sent to a shared Debian 13 print queue, Roundcube email attachments processed when opened, and public WordPress plugin upload forms.
  • Updating only the host operating system may not fix the exposure if an application or container includes its own older Ghostscript copy.

Technologies: cms, operating-system

Products: ghostscript, wordpress-core, imagemagick, pillow, libvips, roundcube, forminator, essential-addons-for-elementor, debian-linux, suse-linux-enterprise, opensuse-leap, apparmor

Vendors: artifex, wordpress, google, imagemagick, roundcube, suse, debian

The Invoice That Told You Not to Use LinkedIn's Address — May Read

A fake LinkedIn invoice used the company’s real address but explicitly told accounts payable not to use it, directing payment instead to an ACH account whose “LinkedIn Corporation” name was not verified. The key lesson is to independently verify vendor bank details through trusted channels before paying any unexpected invoice.

  • A fake LinkedIn Billing invoice for $3,990 was sent to the accounting director of a global commercial real estate firm and requested payment by ACH transfer.
  • The invoice displayed LinkedIn’s real Sunnyvale, California address but twice instructed the recipient not to remit payment to that address.
  • The payment details named a real U.S. bank and listed the account name as “LinkedIn Corporation,” but the article states that ACH credits are generally routed by account and routing number without verifying the account holder’s name.
  • The sender used an unrelated Thai company domain and a display name matching the target firm’s chief executive, while the subject line contained the firm’s name inside unfinished-looking curly braces.
  • The accounting director reported the email as phishing, and a human analyst classified it as malicious and quarantined four copies in the reviewing mailbox.

Technologies: email-security

Products: linkedin-talent-solutions, ironscales

Vendors: linkedin, ironscales

Top Ransomware Gangs & AI Pentesting Tools — Optional

Top ransomware affiliates have not broadly adopted autonomous AI pentesting frameworks because their proven access-broker model and manual Windows/ESXi tradecraft are stealthier, more reliable, and more cost-effective. AI is more likely being used quietly for operator assistance, while smaller crews absorb the expense and OPSEC risks of agentic tooling.

  • The article says established ransomware affiliates such as Akira, Qilin, and Rhysida have not been widely reported using autonomous AI offensive frameworks such as ARTEX, Cairn, or PentAGI.
  • Smaller or newer extortion groups, including WhiteArmor, Settra, and n0n, have been observed experimenting with AI tools, sometimes with poor operational security.
  • Top ransomware affiliates often purchase pre-vetted corporate access from initial access brokers and focus on internal actions such as moving through Windows domains, stealing data, and targeting VMware ESXi systems.
  • The article argues that cloud-based AI services can create logging, account-suspension, attribution, and cost risks, while locally hosting capable models requires expensive hardware and operational effort.
  • SOCRadar reported cases involving INC/Lynx and TheGentlemen affiliates using AI-based frameworks, with reported OpenRouter costs of $4,500 and $23,900 respectively.

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposed Customer Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 19:00 → 21 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets — Should Read

Rackspace Spot was breached using leaked credentials, allowing attackers to impersonate users, deploy unauthorized Kubernetes pods, and access secrets that may contain passwords, API keys, and tokens. Affected customers should rotate exposed credentials and review logs from November 17 for misuse.

  • Rackspace said an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of its Rackspace Spot cloud platform on November 17, 2026.
  • The attackers could act as legitimate users in some customer organizations, create Kubernetes pods, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes.
  • Rackspace warned that any Secret in an affected user’s clusters, along with that user’s Spot API and refresh tokens, could have been exposed.
  • Rackspace revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed unauthorized pods, rotated keys, and restored the Spot service on November 21 after temporarily disabling access.
  • Affected customers were told to reissue tokens, replace automation refresh tokens, obtain new Kubernetes configuration files, rotate stored credentials, and examine relevant logs dating from November 17.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, secrets-manager

Products: rackspace-spot, kubernetes

Vendors: rackspace, platform9, kubernetes

item.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health Data Exposure and BADBOX 3.0 Ad Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 15:00 → 21 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data — Should Read

Microsoft fixed an Entra Connect Health API flaw that attackers exploited to access tenant contact and configuration metadata, including administrator email addresses, but not passwords, tokens, or active cryptographic keys. Affected organizations should watch for targeted phishing, enforce phishing-resistant MFA for privileged accounts, and review Entra logs and Connect Health settings.

  • Microsoft said attackers exploited a vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API to obtain unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level contact and configuration metadata.
  • The exposed data included technical contact and administrator email addresses, tenant IDs and names, initial domain names, country and regional information, Entra license tiers, directory synchronization status, and Connect Health onboarding status.
  • Microsoft said passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, on-premises Active Directory topology details, and Azure subscription information were not exposed.
  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19, 2026, completed its investigation on November 20, and began notifying affected organizations.
  • Microsoft advised organizations to prepare for targeted phishing or social-engineering attempts, use phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for privileged accounts, and review Connect Health configurations and Entra audit and sign-in logs.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, network-monitoring

Products: microsoft-entra-connect-health, microsoft-entra-admin-center, microsoft-entra, azure-service-health

Vendors: microsoft

BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests — Should Read

BADBOX 3.0 rebuilt after prior disruptions and became the largest documented ad-fraud botnet, generating up to 40 billion fraudulent daily ad bid requests through compromised low-cost Android devices. It also covertly enrolls infected devices in residential proxy networks, and researchers warn its operators are likely to adapt again after the latest takedowns.

  • HUMAN reported that BADBOX 3.0 generated roughly 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day at its peak, representing more than 4% of connected-TV traffic observed by its platform.
  • BADBOX 3.0 infects low-cost Android Open Source Project phones, tablets, and streaming TV boxes to run hidden video ads while impersonating legitimate streaming applications.
  • The botnet also enrolled infected devices into 11 residential proxy networks without owners' knowledge, including PXYEDGE, which HUMAN identified as a rebranded successor to IpMoYu.
  • HUMAN linked the operation to a Chinese electronics manufacturer through associated domains, device-specific code checks, a factory-installed TV launcher, and a repository maintainer.
  • HUMAN, Google, and other partners disrupted BADBOX 3.0 infrastructure, but HUMAN warned that the operators are likely to adapt to the latest disruption.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, proxy

Products: android, android-tv, t95-android-tv-box, pxyedge, ipmoyu

Vendors: google, human-security, android-open-source-project
